newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices rise on mill buying.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices rise on mill buying.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Wednesday gained on increasing mill buying, dealers said.

"Increased mill buying particularly among Gujarat varieties lifted prices for Gujarat cotton while Punjab varieties bounced back after recent losses in line with the rally in Gujarat cotton," a dealer said.

In spot deals Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) rose by 100 rupees to 13,700/14,200 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while Gujarat Sankar-4 (long-staple) rose by 400/500 rupees to 16,500/17,500 rupees per candy for the average variety and to 18,000/20,000 rupees per candy for the superior variety.
Sliding arrivals and a shortage of ready stock kept market sentiment firm at the close of the session, dealers said.

Punjab saw-ginned rose by 10 rupees at 1,590/1,690 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while F-414 rose by 10/20 rupees at 1,920/1,945 rupees per maund and Bengal-deshi rose by 10 rupees at 900/935 rupees per maund.
